source.subject: PHYSICS
source.reasoning_observation: Stipulated human heat load5 kW for4 h gives20 kWh; dividing by assumed 0.5 conversion factor yields40 kWh. Real cooling COP is heat removed divided by electrical work, not necessarily ≤1; source's efficiency wording needs model qualification.

target.protected_work: Combine multiple heat-load paths and measured electrical consumption to discriminate cooling-performance models and predict an independent operating interval.
target.decisive_route: Matched room trial has load6 kW, cooler electrical2 kW and zero temperature trend. Another trial adds3 kW load but electrical remains2 kW with measured accumulation1 kW. Test common COP. Shortest valid route: First COP3; second removal8 kW, COP4, so common COP3 fails under specified loads.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Distinguish heat-load balance from electrical-to-heat efficiency

representation_translation.evidence: Coordinate power, time, stored energy and cooling transfer

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Fit cooling coefficient and other load, predict reserved interval

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Cooling COP can exceed one; temperature held constant does not prove no heat transfer

core1a.scientific_construction: For a room at a maintained temperature, its internal energy is approximately constant, so removed heat equals net incoming heat under the stipulated model. People, equipment, sunlight and wall transfers can contribute. A cooling device's coefficient of performance COP_c=Q_removed/W_electric (or ratio of rates in steady conditions) can exceed one because the device transfers energy rather than converts all electrical work into cooling. For a complete cyclic device, heat rejected to surroundings equals heat removed plus electrical work if other terms are negligible. Do not call COP a conventional efficiency bounded by one. In a stylized exercise a supplied conversion ratio may be used as defined. Use kW for rate and kWh for energy. If temperature changes, include stored-energy change rather than applying a steady balance.

core1b.task: A room model maintains constant temperature in two 2-hour trials. Known equipment heat load is2 kW in both; occupancy heat is1 kW in A and4 kW in B. Other common heat leakage L is unknown. Electricity consumed by cooling is3 and5 kWh respectively. Assume one common COP and common L. Infer both from the two observations, predict electrical use in a reserved 3-hour trial with occupancy2.5 kW, and test an exact measured 6.5 kWh.
